terms.meaning: the record of where a number came from and when it was seen
a past match played back as if it were happening, labelled as history
an estimate made ahead of time, not a fact

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the rules and types
sections.what: Loads the freshness and priority rules and the data shapes.
sections.why: Keeps the rules in the config file rather than here.

sections.name: AuthorityOptions, age
sections.title: Options and value age
sections.what: Defines the options: current time, context, live flag and replay flag. Also works out how old a value is, never below zero.
sections.why: The time is passed in rather than read from the clock, so results are repeatable.
sections.watch_out: A timestamp that cannot be read gives an age that is not a number, which never counts as fresh.

sections.name: isFresh
sections.title: Freshness check
sections.what: Says whether a value is young enough for its context.
sections.why: The limits are set in the config file, so this is only a comparison.
sections.watch_out: A value exactly at the limit still counts as fresh.

sections.name: formatAge
sections.title: Age as readable text
sections.what: Turns milliseconds into short text such as seconds, minutes, hours or days.
sections.why: Used in the stale label so users see how old a value is.
sections.watch_out: Values are rounded, so the label is approximate.

sections.name: stateFor
sections.title: Choosing a state
sections.what: Picks the state for one value. Simulation and projection come first, then replay, then stale, then live only if live is enabled and the context is live, otherwise delayed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the order keeps a simulation from ever being labelled live.
sections.watch_out: Replay is checked before freshness, so an old replay is never shown as stale.

sections.name: LABELS
sections.title: Short state labels
sections.what: Gives the short display text for each state.
sections.why: Keeps the wording in one place for the badges.
sections.watch_out: The stale label is built in the present function, so changing the word here will not change the stale badge.

sections.name: present
sections.title: Presenting one value
sections.what: Turns one value into the presented form with value, receipt, state, label and age. With no value, it returns a source pending state.
sections.why: Gives the page one object to display.
sections.watch_out: A pending value has no receipt to show.

sections.name: choose
sections.title: Choosing among candidate sources
sections.what: From several candidates, shows the highest-ranked fresh factual source. If none is fresh, shows the newest factual one, marked stale. Only if no factual source exists does it use simulations or projections.
sections.why: The comment states this order so users see real facts first.
sections.watch_out: An empty candidate list gives a source pending state, which the page must handle.

summary: Decides which data source to show and labels it honestly with its freshness.
purpose: Stops the app from showing old or simulated numbers as current facts.
why: The file header says it picks between sources and labels results honestly, and the labels follow fixed rules.
how: Works out each value's age, checks whether it is fresh for its context, picks a state (live, delayed, historical replay, projection, simulation, stale or pending), builds the label, and for a list of candidates chooses the best fresh factual one, falling back to the newest factual one, then to simulations or projections.
inputs: Sourced values with receipts, plus options: the current time, the context, whether live calls are enabled, and whether this is a replay.
outputs: A presented value with the value, receipt, state, label and age.
risks: Without the live calls setting, nothing is shown as live. The fallback can show a stale value as the best available, marked stale.
debug: Start with the state label. If a value says stale unexpectedly, compare its observed time with now and the freshness limit. If a value is pending, check that candidates were passed in.
